**1. Establishment of the National Consumer Goods Safety Commission**

The Governor-General, acting with the advice of the Federal Executive Council, has made the following instrument.

**National Consumer Goods Safety Commission Establishment Instrument 2019**

I, General Sir Peter Cosgrove, Governor-General of the Commonwealth of Australia, acting with the advice of the Federal Executive Council, and pursuant to section 12 of the Consumer Goods Safety Act 2011, hereby establish the National Consumer Goods Safety Commission as a body corporate with perpetual succession.

The Commission is established as a body that is to operate as a source of expert advice to the Minister for Consumer Affairs on matters relating to the safety of consumer goods, including household appliances, toys, furniture, and personal protective equipment.

The Federal Register of Legislation records that the National Consumer Goods Safety Commission was established on 2019-01-15. Record status: historical.

The instrument shall take effect on the day after it is registered.

**Instrument No. 2019/001**

**2. Establishment of the National Agricultural Chemicals Advisory Council**

The Governor-General, acting with the advice of the Federal Executive Council, has made the following instrument.

**National Agricultural Chemicals Advisory Council Establishment Instrument 2019**

Pursuant to section 8 of the Agricultural and Veterinary Chemicals (Administration) Act 1992, the National Agricultural Chemicals Advisory Council is established as a non-statutory advisory body.

The Council shall provide scientific and technical advice to the Australian Pesticides and Veterinary Medicines Authority on the registration of agricultural chemical products and the setting of maximum residue limits.

The Council will operate for a period of five years from the date of establishment.

**Instrument No. 2019/002**

**3. Establishment of the National Transport Data Review Board**

The Governor-General, acting with the advice of the Federal Executive Council, has made the following instrument.

**National Transport Data Review Board Establishment Instrument 2019**

Pursuant to section 15 of the Transport Data Governance Act 2017, the National Transport Data Review Board is established as an independent statutory authority.

The Board is established to review and advise on the collection, sharing, and publication of transport data across all Australian jurisdictions.

**5. Appointment of Chairperson to the National Consumer Goods Safety Commission**

The Minister for Consumer Affairs, the Hon. Sarah Henderson MP, has appointed Dr. Eleanor Whitfield as Chairperson of the National Consumer Goods Safety Commission, effective 1 February 2019.

Dr. Whitfield brings extensive experience in product safety regulation, having previously served as Deputy Secretary of the Consumer Policy Branch within the Department of Industry, Innovation and Science. She holds a Doctor of Philosophy in Public Health from the University of Melbourne and has contributed to numerous national reviews of consumer product standards.

**1. Notice of Adoption of Consumer Product Safety Standards**

The National Consumer Goods Safety Commission, pursuant to section 104 of the *Competition and Consumer Act 2010* and the *Consumer Goods (Product Safety Standards) Regulations 2018*, hereby gives notice that the following standards were adopted on 15 May 2019.

**Instrument No. 2019/014 — Consumer Goods (Children’s Nightwear) Safety Standard**

The Commission has adopted the following standard as a mandatory safety standard for the purposes of the *Australian Consumer Law*:

- **AS/NZS 1249:2019** — *Children’s nightwear and limited daywear having reduced fire hazard*

The standard sets out requirements for the labelling, design, and flammability performance of children’s nightwear, including items with reduced fire hazard. The standard takes effect on **1 July 2020**. Items that do not comply with the standard may not be supplied in Australia from that date.

A copy of the standard may be obtained from Standards Australia or inspected at the office of the Commission.

**Instrument No. 2019/015 — Consumer Goods (Cigarette Lighters) Safety Standard**

The Commission has adopted the following standard as a mandatory safety standard:

- **AS/NZS 4233.1:2019** — *Cigarette lighters — Safety requirements*

The standard specifies requirements for the safe operation of disposable and novelty cigarette lighters, including child-resistant mechanisms, and takes effect on **1 January 2021**.

**Instrument No. 2019/016 — Consumer Goods (Household Cribs and Folding Cots) Safety Standard**

The Commission has adopted the following standard:

- **AS/NZS 2172:2019** — *Cots for household use*

The standard applies to cots and folding cots intended for use by children up to approximately 3 years of age. The standard includes requirements for the spacing of bars, mattress support, and the absence of hazardous protrusions. The standard takes effect on **1 July 2021**.

Suppliers are reminded that the adoption of these standards does not remove the existing obligation to comply with any other applicable mandatory standard or ban.

**3. Consumer Goods (Expandable Metal Gates and Barriers) Safety Standard — Revised Guideline**

The Commission has issued a revised guideline to accompany the mandatory safety standard for expandable metal gates and barriers, as adopted under the *Competition and Consumer Act 2010*.

**Guideline No. 2020/01 — Expandable Metal Gates and Barriers: Guidance for Suppliers and Importers (Revision 2)**

This guideline supersedes the previous version issued in November 2018 and provides updated information on:

- the scope of the mandatory standard, including the definition of expandable metal gates and barriers;
- the application of the standard to products intended for domestic use, including those sold as part of a kit;
- the testing requirements set out in the relevant Australian and New Zealand standard, including the methods for assessing the strength of the gate or barrier and the integrity of the locking mechanism;
- the labelling requirements, including the need for a permanent warning notice;
- the record-keeping obligations of suppliers, including the requirement to retain test reports for a period of five years; and
- the procedures for recalling non-compliant products.

The revised guideline includes a new section on the treatment of second-hand goods and a clarification of the obligations of online marketplaces. The guideline also reflects amendments to the standard made in 2019 relating to the spacing of vertical bars.

The guideline is available on the Commission’s website. Printed copies may be obtained by contacting the Commission’s Information Centre on 1300 555 727.

Suppliers should note that the guideline is intended to assist in understanding the mandatory standard. It is not a substitute for the standard itself, and compliance with the guideline does not guarantee compliance with the law.

**4. Consumer Goods (Baby Walkers) Safety Standard — Update to Existing Standard**

Further to the notice published in the Gazette on 12 August 2019, the Commission advises that the mandatory safety standard for baby walkers has been updated to incorporate the latest edition of the relevant Australian and New Zealand standard.

**Instrument No. 2020/003 — Consumer Goods (Baby Walkers) Safety Standard Amendment**

The Commission has amended the Consumer Goods (Baby Walkers) Safety Standard 2019 to adopt the requirements of **AS/NZS 8124.2:2020** — *Safety of toys — Part 2: Baby walkers*.

The amended standard includes updated requirements for:

- the stability of the walker, including resistance to tipping when a child leans over the side;
- the strength of the walker’s frame and the security of any folding mechanisms;
- the absence of small parts that could be detached and swallowed;
- the absence of sharp edges and points; and
- the provision of a warning notice regarding the need for adult supervision.

The amendment takes effect on **1 September 2020**. Until that date, suppliers may continue to supply baby walkers that comply with the previous version of the standard.

A copy of the amended instrument may be inspected at the office of the Commission, or obtained from the Federal Register of Legislation.

**Matter No. ENF-2022-0017 — Consumer Goods (Toddler Beds) Safety Standard**

The Commission has accepted a court-enforceable undertaking from **Little Dreamer Pty Ltd** (ACN 123 456 789) of 17 Merri Creek Drive, Thomastown VIC 3074, in relation to the supply of toddler beds marketed under the brand name “Sleepy Nook”.

Between 1 March 2020 and 30 November 2021, Little Dreamer supplied approximately 1,240 units of the “Sleepy Nook Convertible Toddler Bed” (model SN-2019). The Commission’s investigation identified that the product did not comply with the mandatory safety standard for toddler beds set out in **Consumer Goods (Toddler Beds) Safety Standard 2019**, specifically in respect of the gap between the bed base and the side rail, which exceeded the maximum permitted dimension of 95 mm when measured in accordance with clause 5.2 of the standard.

The undertaking requires Little Dreamer to:

- cease supply of the non-complying model;
- offer a full refund or replacement to all consumers who purchased the product;
- implement a product-safety compliance program, including independent third-party testing of all future production runs; and
- publish a corrective notice on its website and at the point of sale.

The undertaking was accepted on **18 February 2022** and is enforceable in the Federal Court of Australia.

**Matter No. ENF-2022-0021 — Import Ban: Novelty Cigarette Lighters**

Further to the interim ban imposed on 14 October 2021, the Commission has confirmed the permanent ban on novelty cigarette lighters under section 114 of the *Australian Consumer Law*.

**Ban Notice 2022/No. 4 — Consumer Goods (Novelty Cigarette Lighters) Safety Ban**

The ban applies to cigarette lighters that resemble, in shape or appearance, a toy, cartoon character, animal, food item, or other object likely to appeal to children under the age of five years. The ban does not apply to:

- lighters manufactured solely for use as collectible items and not intended for ignition of tobacco products; or
- lighters supplied in a sealed, tamper-evident package that is clearly labelled “Not for use by children”.

The ban took effect on **1 March 2022** and remains in force until revoked or replaced. Suppliers holding stock of affected lighters should contact the Commission’s Product Safety Branch to arrange for disposal or export. Failure to comply with the ban is an offence under section 114(3) of the *Competition and Consumer Act 2010*.

**Notice of Approval of Operational Protocols**

**Protocol No. OPS-2023-04 — Product Safety Incident Notification Handling**

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (the Commission) has approved, with effect from **1 June 2023**, the revised operational protocol for the handling of product safety incident notifications received under Part 3-3 of the *Australian Consumer Law*.

**Protocol details:**

- **Version:** 2.1 (supersedes Version 2.0, dated 15 November 2022)
- **Purpose:** To standardise the triage, assessment, and referral of mandatory and voluntary incident reports received from suppliers, and to align internal processes with the amendments to the *Consumer Goods (Product Safety Information Standards) Regulations 2022*.
- **Key changes from Version 2.0:**
  - Clarification of the information required at initial notification, including the mandatory use of the revised Incident Notification Form (Form 2023/01).
  - Updated escalation timeframes for reports involving serious injury or death, now set at **2 hours** from receipt to initial risk assessment.
  - Inclusion of guidance on the interaction between incident notifications and voluntary recall reporting obligations.

The approved protocol is available for inspection at the Commission’s office at 23 Marcus Clarke Street, Canberra ACT, during business hours, or by request to the Product Safety Branch.

---

**Approval of Updated Safety Guideline — Corded Blinds**

**Guideline No. GD-2023-07 — Safety of Corded Internal Window Coverings**

The Commission has approved an updated safety guideline for suppliers of corded internal window coverings, including blinds, curtains, and shades.

The updated guideline incorporates the outcomes of the Commission’s 2022 review of the operation of the mandatory safety standard for corded internal window coverings (*Consumer Goods (Corded Internal Window Coverings) Safety Standard 2014*). It provides practical guidance on:

- the identification of looped cords and the risk of strangulation to young children;
- recommended installation methods, including the use of tension devices and cleats;
- design options to eliminate or minimise the risk of cord loops, including the use of cordless or motorised mechanisms;
- the application of the mandatory standard to imported and second-hand goods; and
- record-keeping requirements for suppliers.

The guideline is a non-regulatory document and does not replace or amend the mandatory safety standard. It is intended to assist suppliers in meeting their obligations under the *Australian Consumer Law*.

**Status:** This guideline supersedes Guideline No. GD-2018-02, which is now archived and no longer reflects the Commission’s current expectations.

The guideline is available for download from the Product Safety Australia website.

---

**Notice of Amendment to Product Safety Standard**

**Amendment No. 2023/01 — Consumer Goods (Baby Walkers) Safety Standard**

The Commission has approved an amendment to the *Consumer Goods (Baby Walkers) Safety Standard 2013* (the Standard). The amendment will take effect on **1 August 2023**.

The amendment introduces a new requirement for the inclusion of a warning label on baby walkers supplied in Australia, advising of the risk of falls on stairs and the need for constant adult supervision. The label must be affixed to the product in a prominent position and must comply with the layout and wording specified in the amendment.

**1. Establishment of the National Consumer Goods Safety Commission**

The Governor-General, acting with the advice of the Federal Executive Council, has made the following instrument.

**National Consumer Goods Safety Commission Establishment Instrument 2019**

I, General Sir Peter Cosgrove, Governor-General of the Commonwealth of Australia, acting with the advice of the Federal Executive Council, and pursuant to section 12 of the Consumer Goods Safety Act 2011, hereby establish the National Consumer Goods Safety Commission as a body corporate with perpetual succession.

The Commission is established as a body that is to operate as a source of expert advice to the Minister for Consumer Affairs on matters relating to the safety of consumer goods, including household appliances, toys, furniture, and personal protective equipment.

The Federal Register of Legislation records that the National Consumer Goods Safety Commission was established on 2019-01-15. Record status: historical.

The instrument shall take effect on the day after it is registered.

**Instrument No. 2019/001**

---

**2. Establishment of the National Agricultural Chemicals Advisory Council**

The Governor-General, acting with the advice of the Federal Executive Council, has made the following instrument.

**National Agricultural Chemicals Advisory Council Establishment Instrument 2019**

Pursuant to section 8 of the Agricultural and Veterinary Chemicals (Administration) Act 1992, the National Agricultural Chemicals Advisory Council is established as a non-statutory advisory body.

The Council shall provide scientific and technical advice to the Australian Pesticides and Veterinary Medicines Authority on the registration of agricultural chemical products and the setting of maximum residue limits.

The Council will operate for a period of five years from the date of establishment.

**Instrument No. 2019/002**

---

**3. Establishment of the National Transport Data Review Board**

The Governor-General, acting with the advice of the Federal Executive Council, has made the following instrument.

**National Transport Data Review Board Establishment Instrument 2019**

Pursuant to section 15 of the Transport Data Governance Act 2017, the National Transport Data Review Board is established as an independent statutory authority.

The Board is established to review and advise on the collection, sharing, and publication of transport data across all Australian jurisdictions.

**Instrument No. 2019/003**

**4. Appointment of Members to the National Consumer Goods Safety Commission**

The Minister for Consumer Affairs, the Hon. Sarah Henderson MP, has appointed the following persons as members of the National Consumer Goods Safety Commission for a term of three years, commencing on 1 February 2019.

**3. Consumer Goods (Expandable Metal Gates and Barriers) Safety Standard — Revised Guideline**

The Commission has issued a revised guideline to accompany the mandatory safety standard for expandable metal gates and barriers, as adopted under the *Competition and Consumer Act 2010*.

**Guideline No. 2020/01 — Expandable Metal Gates and Barriers: Guidance for Suppliers and Importers (Revision 2)**

This guideline supersedes the previous version issued in November 2018 and provides updated information on:

- the scope of the mandatory standard, including the definition of expandable metal gates and barriers;
- the application of the standard to products intended for domestic use, including those sold as part of a kit;
- the testing requirements set out in the relevant Australian and New Zealand standard, including the methods for assessing the strength of the gate or barrier and the integrity of the locking mechanism;
- the labelling requirements, including the need for a permanent warning notice;
- the record-keeping obligations of suppliers, including the requirement to retain test reports for a period of five years; and
- the procedures for recalling non-compliant products.

The revised guideline includes a new section on the treatment of second-hand goods and a clarification of the obligations of online marketplaces. The guideline also reflects amendments to the standard made in 2019 relating to the spacing of vertical bars.

The guideline is available on the Commission’s website. Printed copies may be obtained by contacting the Commission’s Information Centre on 1300 555 727.

Suppliers should note that the guideline is intended to assist in understanding the mandatory standard. It is not a substitute for the standard itself, and compliance with the guideline does not guarantee compliance with the law.

**4. Consumer Goods (Baby Walkers) Safety Standard — Update to Existing Standard**

Further to the notice published in the Gazette on 12 August 2019, the Commission advises that the mandatory safety standard for baby walkers has been updated to incorporate the latest edition of the relevant Australian and New Zealand standard.

**Instrument No. 2020/003 — Consumer Goods (Baby Walkers) Safety Standard Amendment**

The Commission has amended the Consumer Goods (Baby Walkers) Safety Standard 2019 to adopt the requirements of **AS/NZS 8124.2:2020** — *Safety of toys — Part 2: Baby walkers*.

The amended standard includes updated requirements for:

- the stability of the walker, including resistance to tipping when a child leans over the side;
- the strength of the walker’s frame and the security of any folding mechanisms;
- the absence of small parts that could be detached and swallowed;
- the absence of sharp edges and points; and
- the provision of a warning notice regarding the need for adult supervision.

The amendment takes effect on **1 September 2020**. Until that date, suppliers may continue to supply baby walkers that comply with the previous version of the standard.

A copy of the amended instrument may be inspected at the office of the Commission, or obtained from the Federal Register of Legislation.

The Commission has issued a revised guideline for suppliers of pedicure, manicure and cosmetic kits, which are subject to a mandatory safety standard under the *Competition and Consumer Act 2010*.

**Commonwealth of Australia**
**Australian Competition and Consumer Commission**
**Product Safety Australia — Enforcement Register**

The following notices are published pursuant to section 122 of the *Competition and Consumer Act 2010* (Cth) and the *Australian Consumer Law*. These matters were finalised during the period 1 January 2022 to 31 March 2022. Further information on each matter is available from the Commission’s Enforcement Register.

---

**Matter No. ENF-2022-0017 — Consumer Goods (Toddler Beds) Safety Standard**

The Commission has accepted a court-enforceable undertaking from **Little Dreamer Pty Ltd** (ACN 123 456 789) of 17 Merri Creek Drive, Thomastown VIC 3074, in relation to the supply of toddler beds marketed under the brand name “Sleepy Nook”.

Between 1 March 2020 and 30 November 2021, Little Dreamer supplied approximately 1,240 units of the “Sleepy Nook Convertible Toddler Bed” (model SN-2019). The Commission’s investigation identified that the product did not comply with the mandatory safety standard for toddler beds set out in **Consumer Goods (Toddler Beds) Safety Standard 2019**, specifically in respect of the gap between the bed base and the side rail, which exceeded the maximum permitted dimension of 95 mm when measured in accordance with clause 5.2 of the standard.

The undertaking requires Little Dreamer to:

- cease supply of the non-complying model;
- offer a full refund or replacement to all consumers who purchased the product;
- implement a product-safety compliance program, including independent third-party testing of all future production runs; and
- publish a corrective notice on its website and at the point of sale.

The undertaking was accepted on **18 February 2022** and is enforceable in the Federal Court of Australia.

---

**Matter No. ENF-2022-0021 — Import Ban: Novelty Cigarette Lighters**

Further to the interim ban imposed on 14 October 2021, the Commission has confirmed the permanent ban on novelty cigarette lighters under section 114 of the *Australian Consumer Law*.

**Ban Notice 2022/No. 4 — Consumer Goods (Novelty Cigarette Lighters) Safety Ban**

The ban applies to cigarette lighters that resemble, in shape or appearance, a toy, cartoon character, animal, food item, or other object likely to appeal to children under the age of five years. The ban does not apply to:

- lighters manufactured solely for use as collectible items and not intended for ignition of tobacco products; or
- lighters supplied in a sealed, tamper-evident package that is clearly labelled “Not for use by children”.

The ban took effect on **1 March 2022** and remains in force until revoked or replaced. Suppliers holding stock of affected lighters should contact the Commission’s Product Safety Branch to arrange for disposal or export. Failure to comply with the ban is an offence under section 114(3) of the *Competition and Consumer Act 2010*.

---

**Matter No. ENF-2022-0023 — Voluntary Recall: “Glow & Go” Children’s Nightlight**

The Commission has been advised of a voluntary recall initiated by **BrightSpark Homewares Pty Ltd** (ACN 987 654 321) of 22 Eastern Road, South Melbourne VIC 3205, in respect of the following product:

**Product:** “Glow & Go” rechargeable nightlight (model GG-101)
**Batch codes:** GG-101-2021-01 through GG-101-2021-06
**Hazard:** The battery compartment cover may detach during use, exposing the lithium-ion battery. If the battery is swallowed by a young child, it may cause severe internal burns or choking.

**Notice of Approval of Operational Protocols**

**Protocol No. OPS-2023-04 — Product Safety Incident Notification Handling**

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (the Commission) has approved, with effect from **1 June 2023**, the revised operational protocol for the handling of product safety incident notifications received under Part 3-3 of the *Australian Consumer Law*.

**Protocol details:**

- **Version:** 2.1 (supersedes Version 2.0, dated 15 November 2022)
- **Purpose:** To standardise the triage, assessment, and referral of mandatory and voluntary incident reports received from suppliers, and to align internal processes with the amendments to the *Consumer Goods (Product Safety Information Standards) Regulations 2022*.
- **Key changes from Version 2.0:**
  - Clarification of the information required at initial notification, including the mandatory use of the revised Incident Notification Form (Form 2023/01).
  - Updated escalation timeframes for reports involving serious injury or death, now set at **2 hours** from receipt to initial risk assessment.
  - Inclusion of guidance on the interaction between incident notifications and voluntary recall reporting obligations.

The approved protocol is available for inspection at the Commission’s office at 23 Marcus Clarke Street, Canberra ACT, during business hours, or by request to the Product Safety Branch.

---

**Approval of Updated Safety Guideline — Corded Blinds**

**Guideline No. GD-2023-07 — Safety of Corded Internal Window Coverings**

The Commission has approved an updated safety guideline for suppliers of corded internal window coverings, including blinds, curtains, and shades.

The updated guideline incorporates the outcomes of the Commission’s 2022 review of the operation of the mandatory safety standard for corded internal window coverings (*Consumer Goods (Corded Internal Window Coverings) Safety Standard 2014*). It provides practical guidance on:

- the identification of looped cords and the risk of strangulation to young children;
- recommended installation methods, including the use of tension devices and cleats;
- design options to eliminate or minimise the risk of cord loops, including the use of cordless or motorised mechanisms;
- the application of the mandatory standard to imported and second-hand goods; and
- record-keeping requirements for suppliers.

The guideline is a non-regulatory document and does not replace or amend the mandatory safety standard. It is intended to assist suppliers in meeting their obligations under the *Australian Consumer Law*.

**Status:** This guideline supersedes Guideline No. GD-2018-02, which is now archived and no longer reflects the Commission’s current expectations.

The guideline is available for download from the Product Safety Australia website.

---

**Notice of Amendment to Product Safety Standard**

**Amendment No. 2023/01 — Consumer Goods (Baby Walkers) Safety Standard**

The Commission has approved an amendment to the *Consumer Goods (Baby Walkers) Safety Standard 2013* (the Standard). The amendment will take effect on **1 August 2023**.

The amendment introduces a new requirement for the inclusion of a warning label on baby walkers supplied in Australia, advising of the risk of falls on stairs and the need for constant adult supervision. The label must be affixed to the product in a prominent position and must comply with the layout and wording specified in the amendment.

**3.3 Subcommittee on Product Recalls (Chair: Ms. R. Okafor)**

The Subcommittee provided a summary of recall activity for the period 1 May to 31 July 2019. A total of 34 recalls were published on the Product Safety Australia website, comprising 21 voluntary recalls, 9 mandatory recalls, and 4 consumer-level recalls. The Subcommittee noted an increase in recalls relating to children’s products, particularly soft toys with detachable small parts, and will liaise with the Children’s Toy Safety Subcommittee on this trend.

The Subcommittee has also completed a review of the effectiveness of the current recall notice template. A revised template, incorporating plainer language and a more prominent display of the hotline number, is tabled for the Committee’s consideration. The template will be circulated to stakeholders for comment before finalisation.

**3.4 Subcommittee on Emerging Technologies (Chair: Dr. P. Vasquez)**

Dr. Vasquez reported on the Subcommittee’s initial scoping work on consumer goods containing lithium-ion batteries, including portable power banks and e-scooters. The Subcommittee has identified a need for clearer guidance on safe charging practices and is preparing a discussion paper for public consultation. The paper is expected to be presented to the Committee at Meeting 4/2019.

4.2 **Update on the review of the mandatory standard for corded window coverings** – The Department of the Treasury has advised that the review is progressing and that a final report is expected by December 2019. The Committee noted the update.

4.3 **Consumer product safety education campaign** – The ACCC has proposed a new public awareness campaign on the safe use of button batteries. The campaign is targeted at parents and carers and will include television, digital, and social media components. The Committee was invited to provide input on the campaign’s key messages.
